chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi'l-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar. He said: I heard my master al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

Among what God, Mighty and Majestic, confided to Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him) was that He said to him: 'O son of 'Imran, one who claims to love Me has lied, for when the night befalls him, he sleeps away from Me. Does not every lover love seclusion with his beloved? Here I am, O son of 'Imran, watching over My lovers when the night befalls them — I divert their sights from their hearts and place My punishment before their eyes. They address Me as though witnessing Me directly and speak to Me as though in My very presence. O son of 'Imran, grant Me from your heart humility, from your body submission, and from your eyes tears in the darkness of the night, and call upon Me — for you will find Me near and responsive.'

key_terms.الخشوع: Khushu' — deep spiritual humility and reverence of the heart during worship
key_terms.الخضوع: Khudhu' — physical submission and prostration of the body before God
key_terms.الدموع: Tears — weeping in devotion, a sign of sincere love and fear of God
key_terms.خلوة: Seclusion/privacy — the intimate alone-time a lover seeks with the beloved, here symbolizing night worship
key_terms.ناجى: Intimate discourse (munajat) — a private, whispered conversation between God and His prophet, indicating the highest level of spiritual closeness

ai.seo_question: What did God say to Prophet Musa about the sincerity of those who claim to love Him but sleep through the night?
ai.summary: In this hadith qudsi (divine saying), Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports from the intimate discourse (munajat) between God the Almighty and Prophet Musa ibn 'Imran (Moses, peace be upon him). God rebukes those who claim to love Him yet sleep through the night without devoting themselves to worship. He declares that every true lover yearns for seclusion with their beloved, and that He watches over His devoted worshippers when night falls -- diverting their worldly concerns from their hearts, placing the awareness of His punishment before their eyes, so that they address Him as though beholding Him directly and speak to Him as though in His very presence. God then commands Musa to offer humility from his heart, submission from his body, and tears from his eyes in the darkness of the night, promising that whoever does so will find God near and responsive. This teaching was delivered in the context of Shaykh al-Saduq's assemblies and transmitted through the chain of al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar from Imam al-Sadiq.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Sinan narrated to us from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar. He said: I heard my Master al-Sadiq (as) say:

Among that which Allah whispered to Musa b. `Imran (as) was that He said to him: “O son of `Imran! One who alleges that he loves Me yet sleeps away from Me when night befalls him has lied. Doesn’t every lover love to be alone with his beloved? I am here, O son of `Imran, looking at My lovers – when night befalls them, their sights are diverted by their hearts, and they become fixed upon My punishment. So, they address Me as [though] witnessing [Me] and they speak to Me as [though] present [with Me]. O son of `Imran! Grant Me humility in your heart, submission in your body, and tears in your eyes in the darkness of the night. Call to Me, for you will find Me near and responsive.”
